name: e2e
tagline: Open-source TypeScript test runner that mixes fixed Playwright-style steps with AI agent steps for web and mobile apps.
bestFor: Developers who want a free, code-first AI testing framework and already pay for model access
description: e2e is an Apache-2.0 test framework from the team behind TesterArmy. Tests can use exact locators, natural-language goals run by an agent, or both, on Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, iOS simulators and Android emulators. Successful agent steps are cached and replayed without model calls, and the agent takes over again when the app changes. The framework is free; you supply your own model subscription, API key or local model.
pros: Free and open source under Apache 2.0, including commercial use
Web (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) and mobile (iOS simulators, Android emulators) in one runner
Cached agent steps replay without model calls, which cuts cost and run time
CI mode with JUnit output and a GitHub package that posts one PR comment per run
cons: No hosted cloud yet; the vendor says its test infrastructure is planned for 2027
You pay your model provider separately for agent steps and AI assertions
API testing is not described as a feature
freePlanDetails: Whole framework is free and open source (Apache 2.0); model usage is billed by your own provider

plans.name: Open source
plans.notes: Free framework; bring your own model subscription, API key or local model. No paid plan or pricing page exists yet

hq: San Francisco, USA and Warsaw, Poland
integrations: Playwright, GitHub (PR comments), JUnit reports, Claude Code and other coding agents, Kernel and EAS hosted browsers and devices

launch.what: The TesterArmy team launched e2e as an open-source AI testing framework, then announced a EUR 7M round on 2026-11-03; TesterArmy shuts down on 2027-01-15.

name: Bug0
tagline: Managed QA service where an assigned engineer builds Playwright tests on Bug0's AI engine and gates every release.
bestFor: Startups that want end-to-end web coverage run for them at a flat monthly price
description: Bug0 assigns a forward-deployed engineer who plans coverage and builds tests with Bug0's AI engine, which outputs Playwright and TypeScript. Tests run on every pull request through GitHub Actions or other CI and repair themselves when the UI changes, and the engineer reviews failures and files bugs. The managed plan is $2,500 a month, month to month, covering up to 500 user flows. The test engine is also published as a source-available Playwright library.
pros: Published flat price: $2,500 per month, month to month, no annual contract
No charges for test runs, AI credits, infrastructure or engineer hours
Tests are standard Playwright and TypeScript
SOC 2 certified; BAAs available for healthcare
cons: No self-serve plan on the pricing page; the managed plan is the entry price
Mobile and API testing are not described on the site
Coverage above 500 user flows is priced pro rata, and Enterprise is quote-only
trial: Discounted 60-day pilot (price not stated), credited if you continue

plans.name: Bug0 Managed
plans.notes: Flat $2,500 per month, month to month; dedicated engineer, unlimited runs, up to 500 user flows (pro rata beyond), Slack channel, weekly digests. No annual price listed

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Custom pricing for complex stacks, multiple repos or compliance needs; custom SLAs, quarterly reviews, NDAs, security reviews

integrations: GitHub Actions, GitLab, other CI pipelines, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Playwright

launch.what: Bug0 released QA Agent, a source-available Playwright library with plain-English steps, cached replays and self-repair; the managed service opened earlier as an open beta (date not stated).

name: TestSprite
tagline: AI testing agent that writes and runs frontend and backend tests for code produced by AI coding tools.
bestFor: Developers using Cursor, Claude Code or similar tools who want tests generated from inside the IDE
description: TestSprite takes a plain-language description, PRD or ticket, writes end-to-end frontend and backend tests, runs them against the live app and reports failures with a suggested fix. It works through a web app, an open-source CLI, an MCP server and coding-agent plugins, and checks every GitHub pull request. A Free plan includes 150 credits a month, and paid plans start at $19 per seat a month.
pros: Free plan with 150 credits a month and GitHub PR testing on one repo
Low entry price: Starter is $19 a month with the first month free
Tests both browser flows and live APIs
Works inside coding agents through an MCP server and CLI; SOC 2 certified
cons: Credit limits are low on lower tiers (400 on Starter, 800 on Standard)
Mobile app testing is not described on the site
Annual prices are not shown; the page only says annual billing saves 35%
freePlanDetails: 150 credits per month, 1 seat, 1 environment, 30-day run history, GitHub PR auto-test on 1 repo, Slack notifications; no scheduled runs

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: First month free; 400 credits, 1 environment, 3 repos, 30-day history. Page says annual billing saves 35% but does not show the annual price

plans.name: Standard
plans.notes: 800 credits, 3 environments, 5 repos, 90-day history, Jira and Linear, advanced agent model, per-project memory; annual price not shown

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: 1,600 credits, unlimited environments, repos and history, most capable agent model, priority execution; annual price not shown

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Listed as $199+ with a 10-seat minimum and 5,000+ credits; the page does not say whether $199 is per seat. SSO, SCIM, audit logs, single-tenant option, named CSM; also sold on AWS Marketplace

integrations: GitHub, Jira, Linear, Slack, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Trae, AWS Marketplace

launch.what: TestSprite announced a $6.7M seed round led by Trilogy Equity Partners after its MCP-based 2.0 release, citing more than 35,000 users.

name: Thunders
tagline: No-code platform where AI agents write, run and maintain tests for web, mobile, API and desktop apps.
bestFor: QA teams in Europe that need EU data residency and plain-language test authoring
description: Thunders, formerly Thunder Code, turns plain-language requirements into test journeys that AI agents run and repair when the UI changes. It covers web, API, mobile and desktop apps, and adds AI personas for accessibility and security checks. Plans are credit-based: Starter is $479 a month or $375 a month billed yearly, and a 14-day trial includes Pro access. An optional QA-as-a-Service has specialists write and maintain tests.
pros: Web and API testing on all plans; iOS and Android on Pro and up
ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR and EU data residency (Paris) on all plans
14-day trial with full Pro access and 100 credits
Integrates with Jira, Xray, Linear and an MCP server for Claude and Cursor
cons: Entry price is $479 a month ($375 billed yearly) with no free plan
Overage credits cost $1.50 each, more than the included rate
SSO, self-hosting and Playwright export are Enterprise only
trial: 14-day trial with full Pro access and 100 credits; account pauses after if no plan is chosen

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: EUR 399 monthly or EUR 300 billed yearly; 300 credits (up to 30,000 test steps), up to 3 seats, 2 parallel runs, 30-day retention; no mobile; overage $1.50 per credit. Page does not label which figure is monthly vs yearly; higher figure assumed monthly

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: EUR 999 monthly or EUR 800 billed yearly; 1,000 credits (up to 100,000 steps), up to 5 seats, 5 parallel runs, 90-day retention, iOS and Android, roles and hybrid deployment

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Custom credits or flat fee; SSO, self-hosted deployment, static IP, Playwright export and Cypress/Playwright import

integrations: GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira, Xray, Squash TM, Linear, ClickUp, Shortcut, Azure DevOps, Confluence, Notion, Claude, Cursor

launch.what: Thunder Code, now Thunders, came out with a $9M seed round and a live product for web testing, later adding mobile, API and desktop.
